The Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems, effective September 27, 2023, sets non-binding commitments for organizations developing or managing advanced generative AI systems. ([canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/innovation-science-economic-development/news/2023/09/minister-champagne-launches-voluntary-code-of-conduct-relating-to-advanced-generative-ai-systems.html?utm_source=openai))

   Additionally, the Directive on Automated Decision-Making, implemented in 2019, provides guidelines for the ethical and accountable use of AI within the public sector. This directive emphasizes fairness, transparency, and human rights considerations, offering a framework for federal institutions on the responsible implementation and management of AI systems. ([idimt.org](https://idimt.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/IDIMT-2023-proceedings.pdf?utm_source=openai))

   Despite these frameworks, challenges persist in ensuring AI systems are developed and deployed responsibly. The OECD's 2023 report highlights that while some countries have codified AI principles into binding legislative frameworks, Canada has opted for separate regulations to address automated decision systems in public services and AI systems aimed at trade and commerce. ([oecd.org](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2023/10/the-state-of-implementation-of-the-oecd-ai-principles-four-years-on_b9f13b5c/835641c9-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

   - **Invest in Continuous Training:** Provide ongoing education and training for public servants on the ethical use of AI, emphasizing the importance of human oversight and the mitigation of biases.
